title: Singular -us/-ys words changing s to tt
summary: For this -us/-ys family, replace final s with -tta/-ttä: rakkaus (“love”) → rakkautta.
targetSkills: Singular -us/-ys words changing s to tt
objectives: Form the singular partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.

In this selected rakkaus-type family, remove final s and add -tta/-ttä. Keep the preceding vowel length: totuus and ystävyys retain their double vowel. Many nouns naming qualities use this pattern, but meaning or spelling alone is not a reliable rule for every -us/-ys word. Learn the selected membership explicitly.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: Remove final s and add -tta: rakkaus → rakkautta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “love”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.

examples.english: friendship · Remove final s, keep yy; add -ttä
steps: Remove final s, keep yy and add -ttä: ystävyys → ystävyyttä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “friendship”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Remove final s and add -tta: vapaus → vapautta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “freedom”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.

examples.english: truth · Remove final s, keep uu; add -tta
steps: Remove final s, keep uu and add -tta: totuus → totuutta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “truth”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.

examples.english: possibility · Remove final s, keep uu; add -tta
steps: Remove final s, keep uu and add -tta: mahdollisuus → mahdollisuutta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “possibility”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Replace s; do not keep it before -tta/-ttä.
Keep the double vowel when the dictionary form has one.
Do not copy the s-retaining kysymys pattern.
